key_insight: In people at elevated risk for neurodegeneration, a higher baseline Alzheimer's Progression Score predicted a faster increase in VNN-derived brain age gap over follow-up.
engineering_relevance: This suggests longitudinal brain-age models can be used to stratify risk and monitor progression using neuroimaging plus clinical biomarkers.
method: Used a coVariance neural network (VNN) pipeline to estimate brain age gap from neuroimaging data.
Combined brain age gap with Alzheimer's Progression Score (APS) in a longitudinal analysis.
Compared follow-up changes in brain age gap against baseline disease-risk/progression status.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a longitudinal study in a family-history-at-risk cohort, finding that higher baseline progression risk was associated with a larger subsequent increase in brain age gap.
watch_item: The abstract does not report cohort size, external validation, or effect sizes, so generalizability and clinical readiness remain uncertain.
paper_title: Brain Age Gap Progression in Individuals at Risk for Neurodegeneration
